Role resolution priority in _resolve_role() (profile.aviation_role → profile.job_title → profile.role/top-level → default 'pilot') correctly returns 'cabin_crew' when job_title contains 'cabin', and the caller then short-circuits to return {} — verified by flipping Pietro's job_title.

Note: default role fallback is 'pilot' when none of the heuristics match; this means any client without an aviation profile who happens to have a roster with a `layover_*`/`turnaround`/`flight` day_type will receive interventions. That's probably fine for the aviation-vertical target but worth confirming for any non-aviation clients that happen to have a roster.

rca_of_issue: No bugs found in the iter 116 code. One test-authoring pitfall worth documenting: motor's AsyncIOMotorClient re-uses asyncio.get_event_loop() which becomes closed between pytest asyncio.run() calls, producing 'Event loop is closed' on the SECOND flip. Use pymongo (sync) for state flips inside a pytest session, or wrap the flips in a single asyncio.run() with try/finally so restore always runs. The first draft of test_iter116_flight_support_http.py hit this and left Pietro in disabled=true state until the restore snippet was manually run. The rewritten suite uses pymongo and is now robust.
